full_judgment:
8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner during hearing of this revisionl application submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original case and its subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that despite the pre-emptor-opposite party, no.1 during trial of the original case hopelessly failed to discharge her onus in proving her respective case both the courts below without proper sifting of evidence and appreciation of law decided the merit of the case in favour of the pre-emptor arbitrarily which is perverse in the eye of law. The learned Advocate also submits that from the admission of the pre-emptor it is apparent from the face of the record that after her purchase she mutated her name and paid rent separately and similarly the purchaser pre-emptee after mutation separated the jams and paid rent for his land. Secondly, the pre-emption miscellaneous. case is barred by limitation as the data of registration of case kabla is 19.08.1995 under section 60 of the Registration Act, but the pre-emptor filed the original case on 19.03.1997. In this context; it is the contention of the pre-emptor that she was in the dark about the disputed transfer i.e. case kabla dated 30.01.1995 and for the first time sire came to learn about the said transfer from her father on 09 02.1997. Therefore, the burden of proof is heavily lies upon her that she was not in the know about the transfer prior to that. The learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioner in this regard has drawn the attention of mine on the deposition of the pre-emptor as witness no.1. In her testimony she admits that she knew about the case kabla on 06.02.1998 which is entirely overlooked and misread from the sides of both the courts below in their findings and decision. Beside this the witness no. 2 of the pre-emptor opposite party is a formal witness of the case who has got practically no knowledge about the original case. The witness no. 3 is not an independent competent witness of the case as he happens to be the father of the pre-emptor. Therefore, among all the three witnesses from the side of the pre-emptor-opposite party there is none upon whom the respective case of the pre-emptor can stand or there is no such independent, disinterested competent witness who is dependable and the court can safely believe the contention of the pre-emptor. 

 16. Having gone through the materials on record, I find that the pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 though not at all have been able to discharge her onus of proof; even then both the courts below concurrently held that there is no legal embargo in getting pre-emption. It is curious to note that neither the trial court nor the lower appellate court considered the evidence of both the parties in it's true perspective. The witnesses adduced from the side of the pre-emptee-petitioner not at all evaluated by the- courts below in their observation and findings. There has been glaring misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
